lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding

openQuestions: US-R1-001 was a review-round-1 fix story (findings: 1 WARNING, verdict FIXES_PENDING:1, roundsCompleted 1 of maxRounds 3 per prd.json.review). All 6 stories in prd.json (US-001..US-005 plus this fix story) now have passes:true. The next action is another /cam-review pass over the branch, not another implementer story: prd.review.lastVerdict is still 'FIXES_PENDING:1' (stale from before this fix) until the reviewer re-runs and either emits CLEAN or a new round of findings. The orchestrator/sidecar should route to review, not to `cam next` for a fresh story.

The file-size ratchet for src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts was raised 1058->1072 (tracker ref: this story, US-R1-001) to accommodate the ~13-line unconditional logEvent call + explanatory comment added at the plan-escalated terminal in runPlanPhaseWithReplan. Confirmed the file-size gate counts `content.split('\n').length` (= wc -l + 1 for a trailing-newline file), not raw `wc -l`; budgeted to the split-length value (1072), matching the pre-existing patterns.md gotcha about this exact counting convention.

The prior handoff's open question about .cam-ship-stalled.json / .cam-plan-escalated.json missing from .gitignore/templates/.gitignore (noted across US-002 and US-005 handoffs) remains unaddressed. Not in scope for this review-fix story (its finding was scoped narrowly to the missing logEvent call); still worth a future hygiene story per the patterns.md 'Thinning a phase-signal command doc' collateral-surface discipline.
nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 fixed a single reviewer WARNING: US-004's AC2 required the plan phase to emit the structured 'plan-escalated' WorkerEvent UNCONDITIONALLY on the BLOCK->re-plan non-convergence terminal, but no production code path ever constructed a PlanEscalatedEventDetail or called logEvent with kind:'plan-escalated'. The durable marker (writeEscalationMarkerFn, read by US-005's orchestrator boot doc) WAS already written unconditionally, so all marker-focused tests passed and the gap was invisible to bun test. Root cause: the event kind + detail interface were added to src/supervisor/events.ts in US-002 but the emission call site was simply never wired in US-003/US-004. Fix: in runPlanPhaseWithReplan (src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts), immediately after writeMarker(...) and before teardown() on the audit-blocked/MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS-exhausted branch, added `planOpts.logEvent?.({ ts, storyId: undefined, uuid: 'plan-escalation', kind: 'plan-escalated', detail: { issueId: result.issue.id, roundsCompleted } })`. logEvent comes from planOpts (RunPlanPhaseOptions, already destructured minus teardownPlanPanesFn/writeEscalationMarkerFn into planOpts by the existing code), so no new option field was needed -- purely additive, optional-chained (never throws when logEvent is absent, matching the existing backward-compat pattern for every other optional seam in this file). Added 4 new tests to test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts: logEvent fires exactly once with kind 'plan-escalated' on the escalation terminal, detail carries {issueId, roundsCompleted}, NOT fired on the audit-approved (non-escalation) terminal, and backward-compat when logEvent is absent from opts. Quality gates: typecheck ok, bun test 3475 pass / 0 fail / 35 skip (no regressions), full `bun run check:all` green after raising the plan-runner.ts file-size ceiling (1058->1072, tracker ref added to file-size-budget.json _ref per the ratchet-gate pattern in patterns.md). No new external library touched (Step 5.5: lib=none). Next action for the orchestrator/sidecar: dispatch another /cam-review round against this branch to confirm the fix converges to CLEAN (or produces a new, different finding) -- prd.json still shows review.lastVerdict='FIXES_PENDING:1' (stale) until that next review round runs.

officialDocsValidated.summary: US-R1-001 is an internal fix within cam-cli's own event-logging system (WorkerEventLogger / WorkerEvent from src/supervisor/events.ts, both already defined and unit-tested in prior stories of this PRD). No new external npm library or third-party API surface was introduced, upgraded, or exercised; the fix wires an existing, already-typed optional logEvent seam that was simply never called at one terminal branch.
